frontend/src/components/videoapp/useVideoApp.ts:65-68 reads the saved target and falls back to the default for display only; nothing in the file writes `target: "default"` (grep for `stale` and `target: "default"` finds nothing). frontend/src/components/videoapp/__tests__/VideoApp.test.tsx:463-469 now expects readAppPrefs(DRIVE).target to stay "deleted-id". The Video spec docs/specs/video-library-app.md:151-153 (SPEC-CORE-055 failure case) still says "The saved value is replaced by the default." Section 7 of docs/specs/reading-app.md (:218-222) lists only three Video changes: folder base descent, the shown-set Target menu, and the See all sort. Keeping a stale saved id is not one of them. The Reading failure case at reading-app.md:168-170 ("the saved id is left in storage") describes "the app", meaning Reading, and I16a sits under the Reading invariants. Video's behavior therefore now differs from its own unchanged spec text, outside the declared three changes.

specification_compliance: TP-6: Video's handling of a deleted saved target now contradicts docs/specs/video-library-app.md:151-153 (SPEC-CORE-055 failure case), and reading-app.md section 7 does not list this among the three Video changes.

TP-1 to TP-5: the edited files fall outside the declared touch points. Each edit is either the default-preserving `wrap` prop, an implementation of a required change (the Video See all sort), or a mechanical consequence (a fixture count, guard-test allowlists).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Video now keeps a stale saved target id in storage rather than replacing it with default, which differs from the SPEC-CORE-055 failure-case text.
regression_risks: If a smart folder is deleted and a new one later reuses the same id, Video could silently switch to that folder as the target, because the stale id is no longer cleared. Whether ids are ever reused was not checked.
test_coverage: VideoApp.test.tsx:463-473 pins the new keep-the-saved-id behavior for Video, the opposite of what video-library-app.md:153 states.
